justice: Road space is overwhelmingly allocated to fast-moving motor vehicles, with insufficient priority given to pedestrians and non-motorized users.
Construction hoardings occupy large portions of roadside area, further compressing available public space for vulnerable groups.
Lack of barrier-free facilities and accessible curb cuts creates major accessibility barriers for elderly and disabled residents.
safety: Mixed traffic of cars and motorcycles without dedicated separation increases potential collision risks.
Construction zones along both sides create blind spots and unexpected hazards for all road users.
High vehicle travel speeds on this wide arterial road significantly raise pedestrian crossing danger.
livability: Large-scale ongoing construction brings noise, dust and visual disruption to the surrounding environment.
No roadside rest amenities, green recreational spaces or community activity facilities are available.
Lack of active street frontages results in low human activity and limited natural street surveillance.
sustainability: Predominantly impermeable asphalt pavement provides almost no rainwater infiltration capacity.
Limited roadside greenery reduces ecological benefits and heat mitigation performance.
No dedicated infrastructure to encourage green travel modes such as walking and cycling.
aesthetics: Modern high-rise commercial buildings create a grand urban visual impression on the left side.
Continuous construction hoardings and unfinished structures severely damage streetscape visual integrity.
Plain uniform road layout results in a monotonous and rigid visual experience.
comfort: Lack of tree canopy shading results in poor thermal comfort during direct sunlight exposure.
Proximity to high-speed motor vehicle traffic generates constant noise and psychological discomfort.
No resting shelters or buffer zones exist to provide a comfortable outdoor experience for pedestrians.
walkability: Narrow and incomplete pedestrian walkways make walking inconvenient and unsafe.
Long straight road sections with limited safe crossing points severely reduce pedestrian route usability.
Construction occupation and hostile motor vehicle dominated environment strongly discourages walking trips.
bikeability: No exclusive dedicated bicycle lanes are provided along the entire road section.
High speed motor vehicle flow creates an intimidating and unsafe environment for cyclists.
Absence of cycling facilities and route guidance greatly reduces cycling feasibility and convenience.
